summary: Requirements derived from stakeholder interviews for ticket triage summarization, deduplication, prioritization, and customer reporting.

requirements.description: Repeated ticket IDs represent updates; retain only the last occurrence of each ticket ID and filter out any tickets whose latest state is closed.

sources.quote: Repeated IDs are updates: keep the last occurrence, and exclude tickets whose latest state is closed.

acceptance.given: A list of tickets containing multiple entries with identical ticket IDs and varying states
acceptance.then: Only the final occurrence of each ID is preserved, and any ticket whose final state is closed is excluded from the summary

requirements.description: Order open tickets in the triage queue by severity starting with urgent, followed by normal, then low, resolving ties by ticket ID in ascending order.

sources.quote: Urgent open tickets must appear before normal and low tickets; ties should use the ticket ID in ascending order.

acceptance.given: A collection of open tickets with mixed severities and IDs
acceptance.then: The queue contains ticket IDs ordered urgent then normal then low, with ascending alphanumeric ticket IDs breaking ties

requirements.description: Provide a summary counting open tickets partitioned across urgent, normal, and low severities, along with a deduplicated list of affected customer IDs in ascending order.

sources.quote: The summary must count open tickets by severity and list each affected customer once in ascending ID order.

acceptance.given: A list of open tickets across various customers and severity levels
acceptance.then: openCount reflects the total open tickets, bySeverity contains accurate counts for urgent, normal, and low, and customerIds contains unique customer IDs sorted in ascending order

assumptions: Input tickets are provided as an array of objects conforming to the normalizeTicket specification.
String comparisons for customer IDs and tie-breaking ticket IDs use standard ascending lexicographical ordering.
All severity and state strings are case-insensitive and trimmed before categorization.
